item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00202","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C04","C22","C20"],"selected_candidate_label":"C04","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C04 is the immediately preceding postponement of the same Panama Canal toll proclamation and supplies nearly the entire operative drafting framework of the child. Both recite the same statutory authority and original toll increase, identify anticipated congressional consideration as the reason for delay, state that postponement serves the public interest by continuing present tolls, and use virtually identical language to postpone the effective date. The child materially reuses this template while adding the intervening postponement, the House resolution, and a new date. C22 is integral background but created the toll rates rather than the postponement template. C20 has analogous extension machinery but much less shared language and structure.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Whereas section 411 of title 2 of the Canal Zone Code... authorizes the President to prescribe and from time to time change the tolls... and provides that no tolls when so prescribed shall be changed unless six months' notice thereof is given by the President by proclamation","parent_excerpt":"Whereas section 411 of title 2 of the Canal Zone Code... authorizes the President to prescribe and from time to time change the tolls... and provides that no tolls when so prescribed shall be changed unless six months' notice thereof is given by the President by proclamation","explanation":"The child repeats C04's specific statutory recital almost verbatim."},{"child_excerpt":"Whereas it appears consistent with the public interest to postpone the effective date... until September 1, 1949, so as to permit continuance of the present tolls until the Congress shall have had adequate opportunity for consideration of the Committee's report","parent_excerpt":"Whereas it appears consistent with the public interest to postpone the effective date... until April 1, 1949, so as to permit continuance of the present tolls until the Congress shall have had opportunity for such consideration","explanation":"This distinctive rationale-and-purpose clause is reused with the new date and a more specific description of congressional review."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby proclaim that the effective date of the said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 26, 1948, is further postponed to, and shall be, September 1, 1949","parent_excerpt":"do hereby proclaim that the effective date of the said [DIRECTIVE_REFERENCE] of March 26, 1948, is postponed to, and shall be, April 1, 1949","explanation":"The operative provision is nearly identical, with only 'further' and the replacement date added."}]}
